thread:
maya: Hey team, spotted a spike of model-pull failures in the prod-gpu-pool in us-west-2 around 10:20 UTC. Errors look like outbound TCP resets when contacting model-registry.s3.amazonaws.com. Suspect sidecar + SNAT port exhaustion.

infra-bot: [alert] prod-gpu-pool: 45%% model pull failures in 5m window — https://ops.example.com/alerts/9872 :rotating_light:

liam: Can you paste a few of the error lines from the model-puller logs?

maya: Sure — repro from one of the pods: 
```
2027-06-23T10:19:58Z ERROR fetcher: tcp connect failed: ECONNRESET
2027-06-23T10:20:01Z WARN retry: attempt 3/5, upstream reset
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset
```

sergio: Two quick checks: conntrack count on the node and ephemeral port range on the NAT. Run on node: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range`. NAT GW on AWS can run out of ports if many pods get SNATed.

anya: Also check Envoy/sidecar egress config — we had a recent policy that denies outbound unless matched by DestinationRule. If the sidecar is intercepting traffic and then SNATing via default node SNAT, it's double hurting us.

liam: I ran the checks: conntrack: 142k, ip_local_port_range: "32768 60999". NAT logs show ephemeral port allocation near capacity for the single NAT GW EIP.

sergio: That aligns. Short-term mitigation: exclude model-puller pods from sidecar interception or disable outbound interception so traffic bypasses Envoy and goes straight to node NAT (still counts but reduces Envoy overhead). Example annotation to opt-out of istio injection: `sidecar.istio.io/inject: "false"` for the daemonset that pulls models.

maya: Pushed a quick patch to the model-puller DaemonSet to add the annotation (rolling restart).

deploy-bot: Deployment maya/model-puller-daemonset rolled: 12 updated, 0 failed.

liam: That should drop one layer, but still limited by NAT ports. Medium-term: provision an egress gateway with multiple EIPs and route model-registry traffic through it (gives more SNAT ports). We can also add additional NAT Gateways or use NAT instances.

sergio: Example Istio egressgateway VirtualService snippet to route registry traffic via gateway: 
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: model-registry-s3
spec:
  hosts:
  - "model-registry.s3.amazonaws.com"
  ports:
  - number: 443
    name: https
    protocol: TLS
  resolution: DNS
---
kind: VirtualService
spec:
  hosts:
  - "model-registry.s3.amazonaws.com"
  tls:
  - match:
    - port: 443
      sniHosts: ["model-registry.s3.amazonaws.com"]
    route:
    - destination:
        host: istio-egressgateway.istio-system.svc.cluster.local
        port:
          number: 443
```

anya: We also increased the node-level conntrack timeout and bumped ip_local_port_range temporarily to "32768 65535" on the nodes. Command we used: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='32768 65535'` and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`.

maya: After those changes plus the DaemonSet opt-out, model pulls dropped to ~1-2%% failures. Starting egressgateway rollout now.

liam: For long-term reliability, let's: 1) add an egressgateway with at least 3 EIPs per region for heavy model pulls, 2) tag model-registry hosts and route only that traffic through the gateway, 3) add autoscale for egressgateway, 4) add monitoring on NAT port utilization.

sergio: Also add a K8s admission rule to prevent injecting sidecars into pods in the kube-system/critical namespaces for healthchecks, and add a namespace-level annotation `istio.io/egressgateway: "true"` for model-pull namespace.

maya: Filing a follow-up RFC for the egress pattern and cost tradeoffs (NAT GW EIP costs vs managed egress gateway infra). Will include runbook steps for emergency opt-out.

deploy-bot: Alert resolved for prod-gpu-pool (model-puller failures) — incident link https://ops.example.com/incidents/4321 :white_check_mark:

anya: Nice work. Leaving the NAT port bump as a scheduled safe rollback if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks all — marking thread closed once RFC is up.
